trainees.name: Maya Alexandra Carleton
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Fellow
trainees.description: Maya is a postdoctoral researcher in the Field lab. Her current research interests focus on understanding how the retina allocates energy for encoding visual signals and how it may be perturbed in disease.

trainees.name: Alejandro Gallego-Ortega
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Scholar
trainees.description: My research focuses on understanding how retinal diseases, particularly glaucoma, affect the structure and function of retinal ganglion cells, the neurons responsible for transmitting visual information from the retina to the brain. I am particularly interested in how changes in dendritic architecture relate to alterations in their receptive fields—the regions of the visual field that influence neuronal responses to visual stimuli—and how these structural and functional changes may contribute to visual dysfunction in glaucoma.

trainees.name: Yasmine Tani
trainees.title: Staff Research Associate
trainees.description: Yasmine studies different ways to analyze the responses of retinal ganglion cells to varying stimuli, using multi-electrode array recordings. She is particulary interested in contributing to robust analysis pipelines for comparing electrophysiological experiments at different light levels.

trainees.name: Anushka Narasani
trainees.title: Lab Assistant I
trainees.description: Anushka is researching morphological diversity in retinal ganglion cells that project to the superior colliculus, and computational tools to analyze and classify those cells.
